sources.title: G. W. Mackey, Imprimitivity for Representations of Locally Compact Groups I, PNAS 35 (1949) 537-545, complete article (Internet Archive capture of the PubMed Central scan)
sources.locator: Complete article, printed pp. 537-545 (sections 1-5, Theorem 1 and Theorem 2 with proof outline)

contents.name: §2, definition of imprimitivity: a Boolean algebra of projections with the covariance relation and the base M
§3, transitivity of a system and ergodicity of the G-action on the base (null-or-conull formulation)
§3, Theorem 1 (regular orbits: an ergodic system concentrates on a single orbit)
§3, the fact that G acts ergodically on G/Go and that the quasi-invariant class is unique up to equivalence
contents.proof_mapping: The source states ergodicity as a fact in the proof of Theorem 2; the page proves it locally from second countability, compact subsets of positive measure and countable translation covers, and uses the published rho-function theorem for existence of the class.

contents.name: §4, the pair generated by a representation L of Go and a quasi-invariant measure, and its covariance
§4, Theorem 2, existence half: every pair based on G/Go is unitarily equivalent to a generated pair
§4, Theorem 2, uniqueness half: equivalence of generated pairs amounts to equivalence of the inducing representations
§5 covariance and multiplicity reduction; local integration into the commissioned transformation algebra
contents.proof_mapping: The source does not state the transformation-algebra claim. Its covariance setup motivates an independently proved local construction: integrate M_f(g)U_g, apply PVM covariance and Haar/Fubini, and use cutoff/group approximate identities for nondegeneracy. The corrected convolution is f1(h,x)f2(h^-1g,h^-1x).

contents.name: §5, the reduction of the pair to a single multiplicity component and the recovery of L from the field of unitaries
contents.proof_mapping: The source uses the Hahn-Hellinger form of the PVM theorem; the page replaces it by the published separable abelian von Neumann algebra multiplicity model together with the standard-Borel base transport, and proves constancy of the multiplicity from transitivity and ergodicity.

contents.name: §5, the operators B(t) and the almost-everywhere constant operators L_t that give the subgroup representation
contents.proof_mapping: Sunder p.17 explicitly defers the a.e. rigor; Mackey pp.540–541 gives only an outline. The local Haar-lift and Haar-regularization helpers provide the full argument: Fubini trivialization on G, local-measure continuity, constant right-H ratios, Borel-homomorphism continuity and measurable descent. Base-coset evaluation occurs only after a strict representative is constructed.

contents.name: §4, the Stone-von Neumann application and the Heisenberg commutation relations
contents.reason: The pair builds the imprimitivity theorem and its standard models, not the Stone-von Neumann uniqueness theorem or the unbounded Heisenberg relations; those belong to the later group C*-algebra and SL2(R) pairs and are outside this page.

contents.name: §5 Haar-space proof outline: quotient/Haar null-class transfer and measurable descent
contents.proof_mapping: Full local proof extends the published Weil formula to Borel integrands, averages arbitrary quasi-invariant measures, and descends right-H-invariant Borel fields by Haar Fubini. The outline is not cited as a proof.

contents.name: §5 Haar-space proof outline: B(t), constant stabilizer ratios and uniqueness
contents.proof_mapping: Full local pair-groupoid Fubini construction and L0 continuity supply the omitted regularization; right-H ratios define sigma a.e. on Haar G and section-coordinate descent supplies B(x). Source values at a null coset are never used.

sources.title: V. S. Sunder, Notes on the Imprimitivity Theorem (Institute of Mathematical Sciences / Indian Statistical Institute lecture notes, October 1995, 22 pp.)
sources.locator: Sections 2-5, printed pp. 2-21 (measure-theoretic preliminaries; Hahn-Hellinger Theorem 3.7; Fact 1 cross-section; Proposition 4.1 and Theorem 4.3; Theorem 5.1)

contents.name: §2, Proposition 2.4 (translation automorphisms of a measure space give unitary operators)
contents.proof_mapping: The translation unitaries are used in their published rho-measure form (the induced-action unitaries of the RG-23 page); the source formula is the same computation in the abstract measure-space setting.

contents.name: §3, Lemma 3.5-3.6 and Theorem 3.7 (commutant of the multiplication algebra and the Hahn-Hellinger decomposition)
contents.proof_mapping: The page uses the published spectral multiplicity model for separable abelian von Neumann algebras instead of reproving the C0(X) form, and realizes the standard Borel base through a bimeasurable real coding plus the base-transport lemma.

contents.name: §3, uniqueness half of Theorem 3.7 (measure class and multiplicity strata determined up to null sets)
contents.proof_mapping: The page proves the same rigidity on a standard Borel base: localize to constant-multiplicity pieces, write the intertwiner as a matrix of multiplication operators and force equal fibre dimensions.

contents.name: Fact 1, existence of a measurable cross-section s: G/H -> G
contents.proof_mapping: Source Fact 1 states existence without proof. Local nested relatively compact open base sets with shrinking diameters provide an explicit Borel selection: all index tests use the open quotient map, the limit is Borel and lies in the closed fibre.

contents.name: Fact 2, existence and uniqueness up to equivalence of a sigma-finite quasi-invariant measure on G/H
contents.proof_mapping: The normalized existence and the class are supplied by the published rho-function theorem of RG-23; the page only records the class as part of the definition of a transitive system.

contents.name: Proposition 4.1, the canonical induced representation in the covariant model
Theorem 4.3(a)-(b), the imprimitivity theorem with the recovery of U^0 from the system
Theorem 4.3(b) proof, equations (4.4)-(4.7) and the reconstruction B^{-1}U_gB
Theorem 4.3(b) proof, the a.e. constant operators L_t on the base fibre
contents.proof_mapping: Sunder p.17 explicitly defers the a.e. rigor; Mackey pp.540–541 gives only an outline. The local Haar-lift and Haar-regularization helpers provide the full argument: Fubini trivialization on G, local-measure continuity, constant right-H ratios, Borel-homomorphism continuity and measurable descent. Base-coset evaluation occurs only after a strict representative is constructed.

contents.name: §5, the fact that a unitary representation of an abelian group extends to a *-representation of C0 of its dual (SNAG step used for pi|A)
contents.proof_mapping: The source states the extension as a fact. Local proved character-classification, dense-C0 Fourier algebra and C0-PVM bridge now supply every missing spectral input; no recorded unproved remark is a logical prerequisite.

contents.name: §5, Theorem 5.1 (irreducibles of A x K are induced from the little groups of dual orbits)
§5, worked applications of Theorem 5.1 to the examples of semi-direct products
contents.proof_mapping: Direct computation gives one nonzero orbit for the full real dilation group and two for its positive subgroup. The local spectral/diagonal-commutant argument proves irreducibility and spectral supports distinguish the positive-group sign classes, agreeing with Bekka Remark 3.C.6.

contents.name: §5, projective (multiplier) representations and the general non-regular orbit theory
contents.reason: The pair treats ordinary unitary systems of imprimitivity; projective multipliers and non-regular orbit decompositions are outside its scope and are not consumed by any item on either page.

sources.title: G. Misra, E. K. Narayanan and C. Varughese, Mackey Imprimitivity and commuting tuples of homogeneous normal operators, arXiv:2402.15737 (2024, 20 pp.)
sources.locator: Sections 1-4, journal pp. 1-15 (spectral theorem for representations; Definition 4.4; Theorems 4.5-4.6)

contents.name: Definition 4.4, systems of imprimitivity as a representation plus a regular projection-valued measure with the covariance relation
Theorem 4.5, Mackey imprimitivity theorem in canonical multiplier form on L2(G/H, mu; V)
Theorem 4.5 and the multiplier identity after it (the cocycle condition m(g1g2,x)=m(g1,x)m(g2,g1^{-1}x))
contents.proof_mapping: Local joint representatives are constructed by Borel indexed summable L2 approximants of the strongly continuous column sections; the cocycle holds pairwise a.e. The separate Haar regularization helper proves the strict representative required for stabilizer extraction.

contents.name: Theorem 4.5(iii), the explicit canonical action with density and stabilizer factor
contents.proof_mapping: The page derives the same canonical form from the multiplicity model and the cross-section cocycle, with the rho-measure density of the RG-23 convention.

contents.name: Section 1 and Theorems 2.5, the spectral theorem for commuting tuples of homogeneous normal operators
contents.reason: The pair needs only the transitive one-orbit case; the general commuting-tuple machinery and the decomposition of imprimitivities over several orbits are the source's own later topic and are not consumed here.

contents.name: Theorems 4.5-4.6, reduction of a general imprimitivity to direct sums over orbits and the role of transitivity
contents.proof_mapping: The counterexample records the two-orbit situation described by the source: the invariant spectral projections split the system over the orbits, so no single stabilizer classifies the whole base.

contents.name: Chapter 3 §3.C and Remark 3.C.6, the duals of Aff(R) and of the orientation-preserving group Aff(R)_0

alternatives.argument: Definition of a system of imprimitivity as a pair (U,P) with the covariance relation, taken from Mackey §2 (Boolean algebra of projections and the covariance relation) and Misra et al. Definition 4.4; the book version is an equivalent classical formulation.

Local complete covariance/Haar/Fubini calculation against the PVM integral suppliers. Mackey and Sunder do not supply a transformation-algebra proof and Rieffel is not claimed read; source citation is not a proof substitute.

The local Haar regularization helper proves the source cocycle factorization; substituting at g^{-1}x cancels B at source and target and gives the canonical induced action. Sunder equations (4.5)–(4.7) motivate but do not prove measurable closure.

The commissioned theorem is assembled from the proved local multiplicity, joint-cocycle, Haar regularization and reconstruction interfaces. Mackey Theorem 2 supplies the formulation and Haar strategy; Sunder Theorem 4.3 explicitly defers measurable details, now locally proved.

The little-group reduction for abelian normal subgroups, from Sunder Theorem 5.1 (with proof for the semi-direct product case) and from Bekka-de la Harpe Chapter 3 §3.C for the worked affine-group instance.

sources.title: Lynn H. Loomis, An Introduction to Abstract Harmonic Analysis, complete monograph; read §§34A–34C only
sources.locator: §§34A–34C, printed pp.134–137; PDF pp.142–145. Full PDF fetched; these sections actually read.

contents.name: §34A: a nonzero L1 character gives a continuous unitary group character through translates
§34B: classification and integral evaluation of all L1 characters
contents.proof_mapping: Local proof uses the Bochner identity f*k=integral f(n)L_nk, avoiding the source dual-L1 representation argument; exact published Bochner/Fubini and translation suppliers are declared.

contents.name: §34C: weak character topology equals compact-open topology
contents.proof_mapping: Uniform convergence on compact translation orbits follows from finite norm-nets and the automatic bound on character norms; compact-open convergence of integrals follows by controlling L1 tails.

contents.name: Consequences of §§34A–C: Fourier transforms lie in C0 and form a dense self-adjoint algebra
contents.proof_mapping: The entire C0/density argument is local: Banach-Alaoglu on the sum-norm unitization plus character classification and compact Stone-Weierstrass. No Fourier inversion or Pontryagin duality is used.

contents.name: Local C0 representation to PVM bridge for the SNAG application
contents.proof_mapping: Local unitization argument uses the exact published compact C(K)-representation PVM interface; nondegeneracy removes the infinity atom. This is an independently written bridge, not a claimed source theorem in the read range.
